predecessors.name: Kamerun
predecessors.text: the Douala patch of Cliopatria's Kamerun row (1868-1870), which Cliopatria continues in this row from 1871

successors.name: South Africa
successors.text: South West Africa, occupied by South African forces from 9 July 1915 and held as a League of Nations mandate

successors.name: British Africa
successors.text: German East Africa (to Britain 7 May 1919, the Tanganyika mandate) and the north-western fifth of Kamerun on the Nigerian border (British Cameroons)

successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: French Cameroun (about four fifths of Kamerun), French Togoland (about two thirds of Togoland) and Neukamerun, which the Agadir Crisis page says returned to France in 1916

successors.name: British Togoland
successors.text: British Togoland: the Ghana part of Cliopatria's Togoland shape, the British zone from 27 December 1916

successors.name: Belgian Congo
successors.text: Ruanda-Urundi, ceded by Britain to Belgium under the 30 May 1919 agreement (GEA page)

successors.name: Portuguese Mozambique
successors.text: the Kionga Triangle, which 'virtually forced Portugal to cede' in 1894 and which the Commission on Mandates agreed on 12 July 1919 'would be given to Portugal'

capitals.name: Douala (coastal seat of German rule in Kamerun)

ledger.x: 24 April 1884: Bismarck places Angra Pequena under German protection, the first German colony in Africa.
5 July 1884: Nachtigal makes Togoland a German protectorate.
17 August 1884: the Protectorate of Cameroon begins.
1885: the German claim covers all of South West Africa.
27 February 1885: Bismarck's charter founds German East Africa under the German East Africa Company.
28 April 1888: the Sultan leases his mainland coast to the German East Africa Company.
1890: Togoland reaches its inland extent.
1890: Kamerun grows inland.
1890: the seat of German East Africa moves from Bagamoyo to Dar es Salaam.
July 1890: the Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty gives Germany the Caprivi Strip.
1894: Germany takes the Kionga Triangle from Portugal.
1895: Kamerun grows inland during Puttkammer's governorship ('1895 to 1906', 'military campaigns against groups such as the Bali'); the page gives no dated treaty or border.
1898: German control of Rwanda.
1900: German control of Burundi.
1905: Kamerun reaches its northern and eastern hinterland, with slivers of Nigeria and Chad.
4 November 1911: Neukamerun.
4 November 1911: in the same accord Germany ceded 'a small area of territory to the southeast of Fort Lamy' to French Chad.
6 August 1914: the Allies invade Kamerun.
7 August 1914: French and British troops invade Togoland.
7 August 1914: the British share of the Togoland invasion.
15 August 1914: German askari seize Taveta in British East Africa.
26 August 1914: Togoland capitulates.
26 August 1914: the British zone of Togoland capitulates with the rest of the colony ('The colony surrendered on 26 August 1914'); the British Togoland page dates the occupation 27 August 1914.
26 August 1914: French troops hold the east of Togoland.
26 August 1914: British troops hold the west of Togoland.
15 September 1914: the Union of South Africa invades South West Africa.
1915: French and Belgian troops occupy Neukamerun.
9 July 1915: South West Africa surrenders.
9 July 1915: South West Africa passes to Union forces.

1916: British and Belgian columns push into German East Africa proper; 'at the Battle of Tabora on 19 September, the Germans were defeated' and 'by September 1916, the German Central Railway... was fully under British control'.
1916: the occupation of Neukamerun ends in its return to France.
1916: Neukamerun returns to France.
March 1916: the British are back at Taveta.
10 March 1916: the Kamerun campaign ends.
March 1916: the French zone of Kamerun is held.
March 1916: the British zone of Kamerun is held.
18 April 1916: the Belgian Force Publique opens its offensive into Ruanda-Urundi.
April 1916: Portugal retakes the Kionga Triangle.
17 June 1916: Ruanda-Urundi is occupied.
June 1916: Ruanda and Urundi are held by Belgian forces.
28 July 1916: Belgian troops take Kigoma.
23 November 1917: the German force leaves German East Africa.
23 November 1917: Lettow-Vorbeck invades Portuguese Mozambique.
November 1917: the Germans leave the colony and the British hold the rest of German East Africa.
August 1918: the column leaves Mozambique.
August 1918: the German column enters Northern Rhodesia.
25 November 1918: Lettow-Vorbeck surrenders.
28 June 1919: German title to Togoland (French part) ends with the Treaty of Versailles; the occupation stops being an occupation and the successor's tenure follows (loss event below; mandates 1922).

28 June 1919: German title to Togoland (British part) ends with the Treaty of Versailles; the occupation stops being an occupation and the successor's tenure follows (loss event below; mandates 1922).
28 June 1919: German title to South West Africa ends with the Treaty of Versailles; the occupation stops being an occupation and the successor's tenure follows (loss event below; mandates 1922).
28 June 1919: German title to French Kamerun ends with the Treaty of Versailles; the occupation stops being an occupation and the successor's tenure follows (loss event below; mandates 1922).

28 June 1919: German title to the British zone of Kamerun ends with the Treaty of Versailles; the occupation stops being an occupation and the successor's tenure follows (loss event below; mandates 1922).
28 June 1919: German title to the Kionga Triangle ends with the Treaty of Versailles; the occupation stops being an occupation and the successor's tenure follows (loss event below; mandates 1922).
28 June 1919: German title to Ruanda-Urundi ends with the Treaty of Versailles; the occupation stops being an occupation and the successor's tenure follows (loss event below; mandates 1922).
28 June 1919: German title to the Kigoma district ends with the Treaty of Versailles; the occupation stops being an occupation and the successor's tenure follows (loss event below; mandates 1922).
28 June 1919: German title to German East Africa ends with the Treaty of Versailles; the occupation stops being an occupation and the successor's tenure follows (loss event below; mandates 1922).
28 June 1919: Germany renounces South West Africa.
28 June 1919: Germany renounces German East Africa.
1919: Ruanda-Urundi passes to Belgium.
1919: the Kionga Triangle returns to Portugal.
1919: Kamerun is divided between Britain and France.
1919: French Cameroun.
1919: Togoland's British zone.
1919: Togoland's French zone, the Togo part of the colony (the mandate formally dates from 20 July 1922).
28 June 1919: German rule in Africa ends.

wars.name: Abushiri Revolt
wars.outcome: Put down by the Germans with British help; no territory changed hands.

wars.name: Herero and Nama genocide
wars.outcome: German reprisals ended both risings; the colony's borders did not change.

wars.name: Maji Maji Rebellion
wars.outcome: Put down by Governor von Götzen; no territory changed hands.

wars.name: Agadir Crisis
wars.outcome: No fighting. The Franco-German Accord of 4 November 1911 recognised French Morocco and gave Germany the 275,000 km2 of Neukamerun.

wars.name: Togoland campaign
wars.outcome: Allied victory: the colony surrendered on 26 August 1914 after a few skirmishes; British and French zones from 27 December 1916.

wars.name: Kamerun campaign
wars.outcome: Allied victory; Kamerun partitioned along the Picot Provisional Partition Line (February 1916), Britain taking about a fifth; mandates 1919.

wars.name: South West Africa campaign
wars.outcome: Allied (South African) victory; the colony capitulated at Khorab on 9 July 1915 and was administered by South Africa as a mandate from 1919.

wars.name: East African campaign (World War I)
wars.outcome: Allied victory: 'German East Africa partitioned by Britain, Belgium and Portugal'.

certainty.note: Protectorates on coastal stretches and company charters; none of the pages opened gives a boundary.
